title: Radar 1: Punish the Hanging Queen
prompt: White to move. Black got greedy and placed their Queen on g4 without any defender. How do you punish this blunder immediately?
blunderExplanation: Black's Queen on g4 is completely undefended! Either bishop attack or pawn kick wins the queen, but Bishop to g5 (or h3 trapping) punishes Black's early queen excursion immediately.
takeaway: Never make a move until you scan for undefended enemy pieces. In the 400-800 rating range, 1 out of every 4 games contains an undefended queen blunder.

title: Radar 2: The Lethal Knight Fork
prompt: White to move. Black's King on e8 and Rook on a8 are vulnerable. Can your Knight fork king and rook on c7?
blunderExplanation: Nb5 threatens Nc7+, which gives check to the King on e8 while attacking the Rook on a8. Black cannot defend both c7 and keep their pieces safe!
takeaway: Knights are tactical monsters for beginners because their L-shaped jumps can hit two high-value targets at once without being blocked.

title: Radar 3: Back-Rank Checkmate
prompt: White to move. Black's King is trapped behind their own pawns ('pawn shield trap'). Find the crushing 1-move checkmate!
blunderExplanation: Re8+ forces Rxe8, wait: if Re8+, Black has r on d8, so White trades rooks or plays Rd1 / Re8#. When Re8+ is played, Black must take Rxe8, Rxe8# is checkmate! Black's king has no escape square (no 'luft').
takeaway: Always create an escape window ('luft') for your king with h3 or g3 before launching deep attacks, and watch for opponents who forget!
